assumptions: the declared Gamma_1 convention is evaluated for the zero-energy plus-end L2 solution at the finite normalization point Q_0=-4, where c_p(Q_0)=1 and c_p'(Q_0)=0
for real kappa and positive z, K_(i*kappa)(z) and the stated derivative combination are real up to controlled numerical imaginary residue
the fixed-window grid census reports only roots evidenced by a sign change between adjacent grid samples; it is not a proof of absence of tangential, multiple, or sub-grid roots
the p sign is not independently scanned because kappa depends on abs(p); the runner nevertheless records the exact plus/minus-p parity consequence
the zero-shell boundary equation is only a characteristic condition for this declared extension and is not a spectral-density or group-averaging formula
a characteristic-root census does not provide eigenvalue-branch transversality d(lambda_j)/dp, spectral normalization, a rigging-map test space, or delta(C) derivative weights

declared_conventions.p_zero_rule: F(0)=-z_0*K_1(z_0)<0, so p=0 is not a characteristic root
declared_conventions.reference_pair: c_p(Q_0)=1,c_p'(Q_0)=0; Gamma_1,p(u)=-W(u,c_p)|_(Q=Q_0) for a zero-energy solution
declared_conventions.root_definition: a sign-changing adjacent-grid bracket for real F(kappa), refined by bisection; even-multiplicity or sub-grid roots are not ruled out

exact_calculation.boundary_reduction: W(K,c_p)=K*c_p'-partial_Q(K)*c_p=-partial_Q(K) at Q0; Gamma_1,p(K)=-W(K,c_p)=partial_Q K=z*partial_z K at Q0=-4

exact_checks.statement: W(K,c_p)=K*c_p'-partial_Q(K)*c_p=-partial_Q(K) at Q_0, hence Gamma_1(K)=-W(K,c_p)=partial_Q K=z*partial_z K because c_p=1 and c_p'=0
kappa=sqrt(3/2)*abs(p) is exactly invariant under p -> -p at hbar=1
F(0) is strictly negative in the declared positive-z convention
reported roots are strictly ordered and their centers are separated by more than twice the maximum refined bracket width

numerical_calculation.root_definition: a sign-changing adjacent-grid bracket for real F(kappa), refined by bisection; even-multiplicity or sub-grid roots are not ruled out
numerical_calculation.scope: fixed finite-window sign-changing grid census only; no claim about missed tangencies, sub-grid roots, spectral weights, or RAQ

numerical_checks.statement: each reported root has small recurrence-characteristic residual
the recurrence characteristic agrees with an independent centered z derivative at every reported root
every refined sign-changing root bracket is below the fixed width threshold
the real-kappa, positive-z characteristic and independent derivative are real within the declared precision

primary_sources.not_used_for: a raw-C spectral measure, a group average, a rigging map, or a quantum-equivalence theorem
primary_sources.source: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, modified Bessel functions, sections 10.25, 10.29 and 10.40
primary_sources.used_for: the modified-Bessel equation, K_nu derivative recurrence, and positive-real-z asymptotic selection of K_(i*kappa)

primary_sources.not_used_for: claiming that a finite root scan gives a global spectral resolution
primary_sources.source: Weyl, Ueber gewoehnliche Differentialgleichungen mit Singularitaeten und die zugehoerigen Entwicklungen willkuerlicher Funktionen, Math. Ann. 68 (1910) 220-269
primary_sources.used_for: the inherited limit-point statement that the plus end selects one L2 solution up to scale

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: z*d_z K_(i*kappa)(z)=-(z/2)[K_(i*kappa-1)(z)+K_(i*kappa+1)(z)]; the numerical census independently checks this recurrence against a centered z derivative
theorem_guards.hypotheses: z is positive and the order is i*kappa with real kappa; the same analytic K branch is used for all three orders

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: the endpoint Wronskian boundary value may be evaluated at Q0, giving Gamma_1,p(K)=partial_Q K there; this does not identify a literal endpoint value of either solution
theorem_guards.hypotheses: K_(i*kappa)(z(Q)) and c_p(Q) solve the pinned zero-energy fiber equation, and c_p(Q0)=1, c_p'(Q0)=0
theorem_guards.theorem: Wronskian conservation for two solutions of the same zero-energy equation without a first-derivative term

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: K_(i*kappa) is the unique plus-end L2 zero-energy solution up to scale in this declared fiber; this does not provide a full spectral resolution at nonzero spectral parameter
theorem_guards.hypotheses: the pinned raw-C audit identifies the plus endpoint as limit-point and the zero-energy Bessel reduction has K_(i*kappa)(z) decaying while I_(i*kappa)(z) grows for positive z
theorem_guards.theorem: modified-Bessel large-positive-z asymptotics plus inherited limit-point classification

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: F(0)=-z_0*K_1(z_0)<0, so p=0 is not a root of this zero-shell boundary condition; no p=0 atom or sector conclusion follows
theorem_guards.hypotheses: z_0>0 and the characteristic convention is F(0)=z_0*K_0'(z_0)
theorem_guards.theorem: K_0'(z)=-K_1(z) and positivity of K_1 on positive real z

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: the output is a census of sign-changing adjacent-grid brackets only. It does not rule out even-multiplicity, tangential, or sub-grid roots and is not a spectral measure
theorem_guards.hypotheses: the reported window, precision, grid, bisection count and root cap remain fixed; real F values are checked by their numerical imaginary residues
theorem_guards.theorem: sign-change bisection for a continuous real special-function boundary value
